claim.title: Critical exponent in D-dimensional uniform ball model
claim.statement: In the D-dimensional uniform ball model, the test error $E_D(t)$ near the grokking transition scales as $E_D(t) \propto (t_\epsilon - t)^{\frac{D+1}{2}}$, where $D$ is the dimension of the latent space.
claim.test_plan: Simulate the D-dimensional uniform ball model from Section 3.3. Sample $N$ positive and $N$ negative samples from uniform distributions in unit balls shifted by $\pm \epsilon$ along the first axis. Apply a shift to the samples to create a non-typical dataset that exhibits grokking (as described in Section 3.3.1). Train a perceptron $f(\tilde{x}) = \text{sgn}(\tilde{x} \cdot w)$ using gradient descent. Record test error $E(t)$ for $t < t_\epsilon$. Fit the log-log plot of $E(t)$ vs $(t_\epsilon - t)$ to a power law. Pass if the fitted exponent $\nu$ is within 0.1 of $(D+1)/2$ for $D \in \{2, 5, 10\}$.
claim.evidence_in_paper: Section 3.3.1, Eq. 23: 'The critical exponent is hence determined only by the dimensionality of the feature distribution... $E_D(t) \approx ... (t - t_\epsilon)^{\frac{D+1}{2}}$'.
claim.success_criterion: The fitted critical exponent $\nu$ matches the theoretical prediction $(D+1)/2$ within a tolerance of 0.1 for tested dimensions $D$.
